bib.title: Agent S: An Open Agentic Framework that Uses Computers Like a Human

question: How can an MLLM-based GUI agent acquire domain knowledge, plan over long horizons and ground actions in dynamic interfaces to complete desktop computer tasks?
hypothesis: Experience-augmented hierarchical planning (web knowledge plus narrative and episodic memory learned from self-evaluated experience) combined with a language-centric Agent-Computer Interface improves GUI agent success over a plain MLLM agent.
contributions: A new agentic framework integrating experience-augmented hierarchical planning, self-supervised continual memory update and an ACI for MLLM-based GUI agents
An experience-augmented hierarchical planning method using external web knowledge and internal memory
Extending the ACI concept to GUI agents with a set of high-level predefined primitive actions
Experiments on OSWorld establishing new state-of-the-art, and generalisation to WindowsAgentArena

method.summary: Agent S is a training-free agent. A Manager retrieves web knowledge (Perplexica) and narrative memory for a query, fuses them and plans a queue of subtasks; Workers retrieve episodic memory per subtask and emit one grounded action per step through an ACI (accessibility tree with OCR-added elements plus screenshot, bounded action space). A Self-Evaluator summarises successful subtasks into episodic memory and whole tasks into narrative memory, bootstrapped by self-supervised exploration on generated tasks.

datasets.name: OSWorld
datasets.split: full test set; ablations on testsub
datasets.preprocessing: categories OS, Office, Daily, Professional, Workflow

datasets.name: OSWorld testsub
datasets.split: stratified sample of the full test set
datasets.source: sampled by the authors because the OSWorld small set has only 39 tasks, 2 in OS

datasets.name: Self-supervised exploration tasks
datasets.size: top 50 most common tasks per environment-independent generator, plus environment-aware tasks generated from initial OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena environments; total count not stated

other.use: backbone for all ablations, WindowsAgentArena, and one full OSWorld run
second backbone on full OSWorld (Table 1 label 'Claude-3.5'; text says Claude-3-Sonnet in Settings)
adds OCR text blocks to accessibility tree if IOU match finds no existing element

inference.prompting: Manager forms an observation-aware 'How to do X' query; Worker Action Generator emits a structured response (previous action status check, observation analysis, semantic next action, grounded next action); Trajectory Reflector gives advice; one discrete action per step
inference.retrieval: Web: Perplexica search engine. Narrative memory keyed by query Q, episodic memory keyed by <Q, subtask, context>; both retrieved by embedding similarity with text-embedding-3-small; top-k not stated

parameters.narrative_memory_stores: summaries of both successful and failed full-task trajectories with specific actions removed; written by the Self-Evaluator at end of task (all subtasks done or max steps); no human feedback or ground truth
parameters.episodic_memory_stores: complete plan with specific grounding actions for subtasks marked DONE; Self-Evaluator writes a strategy summary after a successful subtask
parameters.action_space: click, type, scroll, hotkey, hold and press, drag and drop, save to buffer, switch applications, wait, done, fail (Table 5)

metrics.name: Success rate
metrics.definition: percentage of tasks completed successfully per OSWorld/WindowsAgentArena evaluation scripts

metrics.name: Error rate
metrics.definition: proportion of failed tasks exhibiting a planning, grounding or execution error

metrics.name: Subtask failure rate
metrics.definition: average percentage of failed subtasks relative to total attempts

baselines: OSWorld agents (Claude-3, Gemini-Pro-1.5, GPT-4V, GPT-4o) with accessibility tree + screenshot
eval.protocol: single reported number per cell; no seeds or significance test stated; ablations on 65-task testsub with GPT-4o

results.claim: Agent S with GPT-4o reaches 20.58% overall on full OSWorld vs 11.21% for the GPT-4o OSWorld baseline (+9.37 points, 83.6% relative).
results.setup: OSWorld full test set, 369 Ubuntu tasks, screenshot + accessibility tree input; backbone GPT-4o; baseline is the OSWorld-reported GPT-4o agent with coordinate-based accessibility tree + screenshots
results.quote: Agent S achieves an overall success rate of 20.58%, nearly doubling the performance of the best corresponding baseline (GPT-4o with 11.21%)

results.claim: Agent S with Claude-3.5-Sonnet reaches 20.48% overall on full OSWorld.
results.setup: OSWorld full test set, 369 Ubuntu tasks, screenshot + accessibility tree input; backbone Claude-3.5-Sonnet; Table 1 labels it 'Agent S w/ Claude-3.5'; baseline row printed as 'Claude-3' (4.41), the best baseline overall is GPT-4V 12.17 and GPT-4o 11.21
results.note: Table 1 baseline rows: Claude-3 4.41, Gemini-Pro-1.5 5.10, GPT-4V 12.17, GPT-4o 11.21. The paper's 'best baseline' text names GPT-4o 11.21 although GPT-4V (12.17) is higher in the table.
results.table: Table 1, row Agent S w/ Claude-3.5, column Overall

results.claim: Abstract states improvement over baseline of 9.37% success rate (83.6% relative).
results.setup: OSWorld full test set, 369 Ubuntu tasks, screenshot + accessibility tree input; GPT-4o
results.note: Text: 'from 11.21% to 20.58%, with a relative improvement of 83.6%'. 9.37 is the difference 20.58-11.21; the abstract calls it 9.37% not points.

limits: Step count and wall-clock time are unaddressed (authors, Future Work).
Ablations only on a 65-task subset, one run, no variance; per-category cells have 6 to 17 tasks.
Only closed models GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet; open smaller models left to future work.
Execution and grounding errors remain most common (Table 3).
Windows comparison uses a similar configuration because the best WindowsAgentArena agent is closed-source.
Hyperparameters (temperature, top-k retrieval, max steps, exploration task count) not stated; prompts not given.
Inconsistencies: Settings text says Claude-3-Sonnet while Table 1 and later text say Claude-3.5; Fig 7 prints 23.18 where Table 7 prints 23.08.
